Results.ReviewText: Bought the 22in Weber kettle since i needed a grill. I went back and forth on getting this or a barrel grill, even tossed around the idea of getting one of the dual grills with propane and charcoal from a different brand. Ultimately went with the kettle as i have had the dual, propane, and other versions of charcoal grills (barrel). I never had any complaints with the last weber kettle i had (still kicking myself for selling it the last time i moved). Might have been feeling a little nostalgic as my dad was in town and he taught me how to grill on a weber kettle when i was 9. The real driving force behind getting a grill at all was my son wanting his 8th grade promotion party to be a BBQ at the park with friends and family. He requested flanken style ribs, his favorite, among other things like burgers, hotdogs, carne asada etc.. the memories of family gathering and listening to the older men in the family tell stories while grilling and shouting for me to cover my ears when they thought i was to young to hear something they had to say came back. It was a great time, surrounded by friends and family telling stories and now being one of the older men telling kids to cover their ears as they watched me do my thing on the grill. Hahaha.. oh how time flies. I don't know for sure, but i think the kettles now hold heat a little better than the last one i had. Simple to use and a great grill to teach basics of grilling to your children (as previously stated, my dad showed me on a weber kettle back in the 90s and i taught 4 of my 5 kids on my last kettle.. the baby of the family will learn on this one). For sure the ash catcher is a great improvement over the old saucer pan thing i had on my last one. The hinged grill grate are pretty clutch too. The color of the grill is awesome too. I wanted a red one (thats what my dad had, and like i said.. i was probably feeling a bit nostalgic since he was in town..) but i saw the copper and since it was in stock and nobody near me had a red one i grabbed it, and i am glad i did.

Results.ReviewText: I tried a charcoal grill years ago. It was a cheap grill that was hard to keep lit, never held a temperature, and was a pain to clean. I swore off charcoal and went gas. This father's day I had a wild hair and wanted to try a "real" charcoal grill. I couldn't be happier! The kettle is very easy to light, keep a solid temperature, and only takes a few moments to clean up for the next session. I wish I'd started with a Weber Kettle all those years back! The flavor is so much better!

14401001.Description: Some things never go out of style—like the smoky flavor of charcoal, the sizzle of a summer cookout, and the iconic silhouette of the 22" Original Kettle® Premium Charcoal Grill. This grill features a built-in lid thermometer to monitor the temperature inside the grill, and a hinged, plated-steel cooking grate flips up on either side allowing you to easily add more fuel while cooking. Like all Weber® kettles, it’s built to last with a porcelain-enameled bowl and lid that retains heat and resist rust, peeling, and scratching, and adjustable lid and bowl dampers to fine-tune the heat for perfect results. When it’s time to clean up, the One-Touch™ cleaning system makes it neat and effortless—just swipe the lever to clear ashes into the enclosed, high-capacity ash catcher. Two wheels make it easy to roll this timeless classic to the center of the action, right where it belongs.
